title: Energy Transmission Across Holographic Conformal Interfaces in General Dimensions
authors: Igal Arav, Theodore Bertrand, Shira Chapman, Giuseppe Policastro, Sebastian Waeber
abstract: Energy transport across conformal interfaces is universal in two spacetime dimensions, but its higher-dimensional counterpart has remained largely unexplored. In higher dimensions, scattering can depend on additional kinematic data, such as the angle of incidence, and conformal symmetry is far less restrictive. We use gravitational holography to study this problem. For a broad class of AdS$_d$-sliced domain-wall geometries, we derive a closed-form expression for the energy transmission coefficient in terms of the bulk warp factor. Our formula reproduces known two-dimensional holographic results and extends them to arbitrary dimension. Within this class, we establish different aspects of higher-dimensional universality. In particular, we show that the transmission is independent of the incidence angle and of the profile of the incident perturbation. We also derive bounds on transmission controlled by central-charge-like quantities characterizing the number of degrees of freedom of the theories on the two sides of the interface. This provides the first explicit result for reflection and transmission across conformal interfaces in higher dimensions, where no CFT-based results are currently available.
summary: This theoretical paper uses AdS/CFT holography to calculate how energy is transmitted across interfaces separating different quantum field theories in dimensions higher than two. It derives a general formula for the transmission coefficient, establishing a new result for higher-dimensional systems and demonstrating surprising universality in the result.
main_problem: The paper investigates the universal behavior of energy transmission across holographic conformal interfaces in general spacetime dimensions ($d>2$). It seeks to extend known 2D results to higher dimensions where scattering is more complex.
main_result: The authors derive a closed-form expression for the energy transmission coefficient, showing it is independent of the incidence angle and the profile of the incident perturbation within the studied class of geometries.
method: The calculation employs gravitational holography, perturbing the metric and matter fields around a domain-wall geometry dual to an Interacting Conformal Field Theory (ICFT). The transmission coefficient is derived by analyzing the energy flux observable.
model_or_system: The model involves a codimension-one defect separating two CFTs, dual to an AdS$_d$-sliced domain-wall geometry. Specific examples include the thin-brane model and Janus geometries.
key_observables: Energy transmission coefficient ($T_{L,R}$), stress-tensor two-point function coefficients ($C_{T,L,R}$), and the energy flux observable $E$.
important_parameters: The dimensionality $d$, the warp factor $a(y)$, and the tension parameters ($\Sigma$) characterizing the interface.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to a broad class of AdS$_d$-sliced domain-wall geometries, and the calculation relies on treating sources as small perturbations ($\mathcal{O}(\epsilon)$).
figures_summary: The notes mention figures illustrating the thin-brane transmission coefficient versus tension, showing both symmetric and asymmetric cases.
paper_structure: The paper develops the calculation by first establishing the general metric and stress tensor VEVs using Fefferman-Graham expansions, then applying matching and scattering conditions at the interface to derive the final ratio for the transmission coefficient.
why_interesting: While highly technical, the concept of energy transport across boundaries is fundamental to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics and open quantum systems, providing a holographic tool to calculate transport coefficients.
